item.title: Rockets are scaling faster than the infrastructure beneath them
item.description: Western launch capacity is usually discussed in terms of rockets: how many, how reusable, how cheap. Those questions still matter, but they are increasingly not the ones setting the pace. In 2021, 36 rockets launched from Cape Canaveral . Last year it was 110, with another 65 from Vandenberg, and the Space Force has said the two ranges could see up to 3,000 launches a year by 2036. Much of that growth has run through ground infrastructure built decades ago. As reusable rockets start to behave more like transportation assets, the infrastructure beneath them will need to make the same transition.

item.title: Space exploration should learn from deep sea technology
item.description: When the Artemis astronauts step onto the lunar surface, they will have spent considerable time and effort installing themselves in their bulky, heavy spacesuits. They will lumber onto the surface having limited mobility and time, struggling to accomplish their assigned tasks. Their activities will kick up clinging, razor-sharp lunar dust that they will invariably carry back into their capsule on their suits. And they will enter that capsule exhausted, perhaps even injured.
